plan.summary:
Links now store their folder in a new `folder_id` column, so the folder view needs no join.

- A new migration adds the nullable `folder_id` column and an index on it.
- `move_link` writes `folder_id` together with the `dirty` flag.
- The `Link` protobuf message gets a `folder_id` field.
- A comment in the original links migration is reworded.
plan.riskRationale: The change adds a schema column and a write path. Existing rows get a NULL folder_id, and the migration has no backfill. No tests are shown.
plan.storyArc: The PR caches the folder on each link. First the schema gains the column and index. Then the write path fills it. Last, the API contract exposes it.

noise.reason: Comment-only rewording of an old migration header. No runtime or schema effect.

topics.title: Add folder_id column and index to links
topics.narrativeBrief: What schema change lets the folder view skip a join? Check that the column is nullable, that the index exists, and that no backfill is present.

topics.title: Write folder_id when a link moves
dependsOn: Add folder_id column and index to links
topics.narrativeBrief: How does `move_link` keep the cached folder current? Verify that `folder_id` and `dirty` are set in one UPDATE, and that the bind order matches the SQL placeholders.

topics.title: Expose folder_id in the Link message
dependsOn: Add folder_id column and index to links
topics.narrativeBrief: What does the API contract gain? Verify that field number 3 is new and that an empty string means the root, as the comment says. Check whether any code fills this field.
